subsystems.name: Contact plate and interface
subsystems.role: picks heat up from the processor's metal lid with as little resistance as possible.

subsystems.name: Heat spreader
subsystems.role: moves heat sideways away from the small contact patch to a larger area.

subsystems.name: Fin stack
subsystems.role: the surface area that air is blown across.

subsystems.name: Fan and airflow path
subsystems.role: replaces the warmed air layer around the fins.

subsystems.name: Liquid loop (alternative)
subsystems.role: carries heat by pumped coolant to a remote radiator.

subsystems.name: Mounting and control
subsystems.role: holds the cooler at the right pressure and matches fan speed to heat load.

buildSteps.title: Set the thermal target
buildSteps.detail: Design to a heat load in watts and a desired temperature rise above room air, expressed as a thermal resistance in °C per watt.

buildSteps.title: Form the cold plate
buildSteps.detail: A copper block is machined flat, then skimmed and lapped so contact is measured in micrometres.

buildSteps.title: Make the heat pipes
buildSteps.detail: Copper tube is filled with a sintered or grooved wick, evacuated, charged with a small amount of water or another working fluid, and sealed.

buildSteps.title: Bond pipes to fins and base
buildSteps.detail: Pipes are pressed into the cold plate, then threaded through hundreds of stamped fins and soldered in a furnace so every joint conducts.

buildSteps.title: Balance and assemble the fan
buildSteps.detail: Blades are injection-moulded, the rotor is balanced, the bearing is fitted and the motor is wired to a speed controller.

buildSteps.title: Finish and test
buildSteps.detail: Nickel plating, a pre-applied paste or pad, and a run on a heated test rig to measure thermal resistance and noise.

buildSteps.title: Install and tune
buildSteps.detail: The cooler is clamped to the socket with even pressure, then the fan curve is set so it stays quiet at idle and ramps up under load.

prerequisites.tech: Heat pipe and vapour chamber manufacture
prerequisites.why: the reason a small air cooler can shed 150 W without a large temperature penalty.
flatness and joint quality set how much heat actually crosses the contact patch.
microscopic air gaps between metal surfaces would otherwise act as insulation.
cooling only works if air keeps moving, and users reject loud machines.
needed for very high heat-flux chips; still being engineered for reliability at scale.

pathway.milestone: air coolers and sealed liquid coolers that handle 150–250 W
pathway.unlocks: reliable performance for desktop and server processors.

pathway.milestone: direct-to-chip liquid cooling for dense AI racks
pathway.unlocks: removing hundreds of watts per chip with warm water, cutting cooling energy.
whole servers submerged in a non-conducting fluid, no fans at all.

pathway.milestone: cooling built into the chip package itself
pathway.unlocks: microfluidic channels in the silicon or lid, pushing the limit of how fast a processor can run.
